title: Morphisms to an algebraic space satisfy fpqc descent
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $E$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $T$ be an $S$-scheme and $\{v_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ an fpqc covering of schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For every family of $S$-morphisms $e_i:T_i\to E$ such that $e_i\circ\operatorname{pr}_1=e_j\circ\operatorname{pr}_2$ on $T_i\times_TT_j$ for all $i,j$ [def-pc-fibre-product], there is a unique $S$-morphism $e:T\to E$ with $e\circ v_i=e_i$ for every $i$. In particular, two $S$-morphisms from $T$ to $E$ are equal if they agree on this covering. No separatedness or finiteness assumption on $E$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04P2, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms: the displayed equalizer of morphism sets, specialized to scheme domains.

proof.text: First prove uniqueness for any fpqc covering of any $S$-scheme $T$. For $a,b:T\to E$ agreeing on the covering, form the sheaf $P=T\times_{(a,b),E\times E,\Delta_E}E$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space] it is represented by a scheme. The projection $p:P\to T$ is a monomorphism: a section above a given test map to $T$ is precisely an equality between its composites with $a,b$, so it is unique. The local equalities supply scheme maps $r_i:T_i\to P$. On each $T_i\times_TT_j$ their composites to $T$ agree; monicity of $p$ makes the maps to $P$ agree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] with target $P$ to obtain $r:T\to P$. Its composite $pr$ is the identity, because both maps restrict to $v_i$ and the same lemma gives uniqueness for target $T$. The defining equality on $P$, pulled back by $r$, gives $a=b$. This proves injectivity without separatedness of $E$.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proposition-sheaf-fpqc, Gabber proof; scheme-domain case cited by Tag 04P2 in spaces-descent.tex.

proof.text: To apply an absolute presheaf criterion to our relative space, define $H(A)$, for an arbitrary scheme $A$, to be the set of pairs $(s,x)$ with $s:A\to S$ and $x\in E(A,s)$; restrictions are composition in $s$ and restriction in $E$. Here $E(A,s)$ is evaluation of the fppf sheaf defining $E$ on the $S$-scheme $(A,s)$. This is a presheaf in the size convention of the algebraic-space definition. It is a Zariski sheaf: compatible maps $s_j:A_j\to S$ glue uniquely, since their continuous maps glue and their local maps of structure sheaves glue and remain local on stalks. After this gluing, the $x_j$ are sections on one fixed $S$-scheme and glue uniquely by the fppf sheaf property of $E$; an open covering is an fppf covering. This also handles the empty covering. Thus [lem-a1-fpqc-sheaf-affine-criterion] reduces existence for $H$ to singleton fpqc covers of affine schemes. For such a cover $f:T\prime\to T$, a compatible $(s\prime,c)\in H(T\prime)$ has $s\prime p_0=s\prime p_1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] gives a unique $s:T\to S$ with $sf=s\prime$. It remains to descend $c$ as a morphism to $E$ over this fixed $S$-structure. Uniqueness follows from step 1, after uniqueness of $s$.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proposition-sheaf-fpqc, Gabber proof; scheme-domain case cited by Tag 04P2 in spaces-descent.tex.

proof.text: Fix such $f:T\prime\to T$ and $c:T\prime\to E$ with $cp_0=cp_1$. The affine scheme $T\prime$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-a1-qc-map-affine-etale-neighbourhood] to obtain an affine $U$, a representable etale map $u:U\to E$, and a scheme $V=T\prime\times_EU$ whose projection to $T\prime$ is surjective, etale, separated and locally quasi-finite. Put $D=T\prime\times_TT\prime$. Both $p_0^*V$ and $p_1^*V$ identify with $D\times_{E,cp_0}U=D\times_{E,cp_1}U$. Use the resulting isomorphism $\phi:p_0^*V\to p_1^*V$ as descent datum: it changes the displayed $T\prime$ coordinate and keeps the $U$ coordinate. On $T\prime\times_TT\prime\times_TT\prime$, both $\phi_{12}\phi_{01}$ and $\phi_{02}$ keep the same $U$ coordinate and the same three base coordinates, so they are equal by the fibre-product universal property. This verifies the cocycle rather than merely asserting a canonical datum.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proposition-sheaf-fpqc, Gabber proof; scheme-domain case cited by Tag 04P2 in spaces-descent.tex.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-separated-lqf-fpqc-effective-descent] this datum is effective: choose $p:W\to T$ and $\alpha:W\times_TT\prime\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ inducing $\phi$. Its hypotheses hold by step 3; in particular no quasi-compactness of $V$ is needed. The base change of $p$ to $T\prime$ is etale, so [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] makes $p$ etale. It is surjective as well: for each $t\in T$, the fpqc covering $f$ supplies a point $t\prime$ over $t$, and surjectivity of $V\to T\prime$ supplies a point of $V$ over $t\prime$; its image in $W$ lies over $t$. Thus $W\to T$ is an etale surjection.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proposition-sheaf-fpqc, Gabber proof; scheme-domain case cited by Tag 04P2 in spaces-descent.tex.

proof.text: Write $W\prime=W\times_TT\prime$ and let $b\prime:W\prime\xrightarrow{\alpha}V\to U$. On $W\times_TD$, the two pullbacks of $\alpha$ differ by $\phi$, while $V\to U$ is unchanged by $\phi$ as constructed in step 3. Therefore $b\prime\circ(1_W,p_0)=b\prime\circ(1_W,p_1)$. The covering $W\prime\to W$ is fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], applied to the scheme target $U$, there is a unique $b:W\to U$ pulling back to $b\prime$. It is an $S$-map: the two maps $W\to S$ given by its composite with $U\to S$ and by $W\to T\to S$ agree on $W\prime$, so the same scheme descent uniqueness makes them equal. Set $a\prime=u b:W\to E$. Then on $W\prime$ its pullback equals $c$ composed with $W\prime\to T\prime$, by the defining fibre-product equation of $V$.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proposition-sheaf-fpqc, Gabber proof; scheme-domain case cited by Tag 04P2 in spaces-descent.tex.

proof.text: On $R=W\times_TW$ the two maps $a\prime\operatorname{pr}_0,a\prime\operatorname{pr}_1:R\to E$ agree after the fpqc cover $R\times_TT\prime\to R$ supplied by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]: both become $c$ composed with the projection to $T\prime$, by step 5. Step 1 therefore makes them equal on $R$. Since $W\to T$ is a surjective etale morphism, it is an fppf covering (etale means flat and locally of finite presentation). By the fppf sheaf condition in [def-trf-algebraic-space], $a\prime$ glues to $a:T\to E$. To verify $af=c$, pull back along $V\simeq W\times_TT\prime\to T\prime$, a surjective etale, hence fppf, covering. There $af$ and $c$ agree by step 5. The uniqueness part of the fppf sheaf condition gives $af=c$ on $T\prime$. Step 1 gives uniqueness of $a$.

source.place: Tag 0APL, proposition-sheaf-fpqc, Gabber proof; scheme-domain case cited by Tag 04P2 in spaces-descent.tex.

proof.text: Steps 3–6 prove the singleton affine condition for $H$ required in step 2. Its Zariski sheaf property and [lem-a1-fpqc-sheaf-affine-criterion] therefore give the sheaf condition for every fpqc family. Apply this to the sections $(s v_i,e_i)$ of $H(T_i)$, where $s:T\to S$ is the prescribed structure morphism of the item. The glued pair $(t,e)$ has $t v_i=s v_i$ for all $i$, hence $t=s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] with scheme target $S$. Consequently $e$ is an $S$-morphism and has exactly the specified restrictions. Step 1 gives its uniqueness and the final assertion about equality of two morphisms. Only the auxiliary chart and its projection were separated; no separatedness or finiteness property of $E$ has been used.

Step 2: the presheaf of pairs H is a Zariski sheaf, which is the 'little argument omitted' in 0APL. H is defined on all schemes while E lives on the chosen fppf site; I accept that as the standard size identification. Steps 3-6: the descent datum on V=T'xU keeps the U coordinate, the cocycle holds by the universal property, W is effective, and W->T is etale by fpqc descent and surjective by a pointwise argument. b descends and is an S-map. The two pullbacks agree on R by step 1, the result glues along the fppf cover W->T, and af=c is checked on V->T'. Step 7 recovers the S-structure through descent uniqueness. New nodes: the affine criterion is an exact P=Flat specialization of isSheaf_type_propQCTopology_iff, with the needed instances present; the affine etale neighbourhood selection is true by 03BX/03FX/03FZ/03H4/03WS; separated locally quasi-finite fpqc effectivity is true by 0AP9+0APK. The closures of the other off-unit citations reach neither chapter. I accept the three declared tool_uses as generic tools: fpqc-representable-descent, fpqc-covering-base-change and fpqc-descend-etale. No fixes.
